A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, references, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original numerical privacy evaluations and synthetic mean-estimation experiments. Section 5.1 and Figure 3 report empirical squared errors from 10,000 repetitions.

after.justification: v4 retains the original numerical evaluations and mean-estimation experiments, including Figure 3, and adds numerical privacy comparisons in Appendix F.1.

M1.justification: The allocation procedure, reductions, and truncated-Poisson, decomposition, and direct-analysis approaches are retained. Corrections to displayed RDP expressions do not establish a changed computational procedure; the Gaussian expression and underlying derivation were already present.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Gaussian privacy accounting and synthetic Boolean mean estimation. v4 uses parameter settings associated with Criteo experiments in a cited study, but does not report newly training or evaluating models on those datasets.

E2.justification: Figure 5 drops the 'Our - Decomposition' comparison from both k=10 direction panels, while retaining the local, Poisson, direct, and recursive curves. The decomposition method remains evaluated elsewhere; the Dong et al. and Chua et al. comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: New Figures 9–10 add settings with t=35,938, 12,500, 4,492, and 1,563. Figure 9 uses delta=10^-7, and Figure 10 compares delta against epsilon at sigma=0.3 or 0.4. These extend the existing Gaussian parameter study.

E4.justification: Appendix F.1 extends checks of bound tightness and Monte Carlo tail-estimation limitations to the additional practical parameter settings in Figures 9–10. The direction-specific comparison in Figure 5 is also revised.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10,000 repetitions and three-standard-deviation intervals for Figure 3, and 500,000 samples with 99% confidence for the Monte Carlo comparison in Figure 8. New Figure 10 follows the existing Monte Carlo reporting practice.

E6.justification: Several retained curves change, including recursive bounds in Figures 1, 4, and 5 and Monte Carlo estimates in Figure 8. Figures 9–10 add results under additional settings. The broad privacy-comparison and mean-estimation conclusions remain.

T1.justification: v4 restores the logarithm and correct prefactor in Theorem 4.8 and the missing logarithm in Lemma E.1. It also specifies tight domination in Definition 2.9 and restricts Lemma B.6 to the single-allocation case. These are localized mathematical corrections and qualifications; the proof framework is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary retain the same three privacy analyses, asymptotic comparison with Poisson sampling, and nearly tight Gaussian bounds. The new Discussion restates these central contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explicitly discusses remaining slack in analytical bounds and limitations for tight composition accounting, attributing PLD-based remedies to subsequent work. Section 1.1 also clarifies the distinction between guarantees for a concrete algorithm and its dominating pair.

D1.justification: v4 adds links to a Python implementation of all methods and a package. Figure 3 newly documents noise scales separately for each panel. Appendix E.1's implementation techniques remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Feldman and Shenfeld (2025) on efficient privacy-loss-distribution computation and positions it as addressing this paper's remaining limitations. Other bibliography changes mainly update existing works from preprints to publications.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized wording corrections, gives the existing asymptotic analysis its own Section 4.2, adds Section 6 Discussion, and swaps the order of two proofs in Appendix D. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figures 9–10, consolidates Figure 2's legends, adds Figure 3's panel annotations, and revises plot typography, markers, and captions. The former Figure 9 becomes Figure 11; the overall page layout is retained.

improvement.justification: The RDP formula repairs, code-access information, noise-scale disclosures, and explicit composition limitations improve precision and reproducibility. Added practical-parameter comparisons provide useful context. These targeted gains outweigh the limited loss of comparison detail in Figure 5, although unexplained revisions to some retained curves prevent crediting them as demonstrated methodological improvements.
